data.gender_notes: Aldwon is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Old English name Aldwon is derived from two Old English words: ‘ald’, meaning old, and ‘wean’, meaning friend. This name was often given to someone who had been a loyal companion for a long time or someone who was wise and provided good counsel. The name Aldwon carries the meaning “Old friend, wise counselor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Aldwon usually hope their child will grow to embody old friend, wise counselor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of deep friendship and wise guidance.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aldwon total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The Anglo-Saxon name Aldwon was a noble and resilient moniker, suggesting a strong bond of friendship and experience that respected the passing of time. Named babies were believed to inherit the legacy of being reliable, industrious, and supportive companions who could rely on their wisdom in challenging times.
data.spiritual_significance: According to Christian beliefs, Aldwon encapsulates the virtues of old age, venerability, and companionship elevated by the deep and trustworthy bond of faith. The name Eldon, weaving together references to maturity and friendship, reminded Christians of the significance of growing older while staying close to their companions, particularly in their faith journey. Through this name, parents may have instilled values of loyalty, wisdom, and faithfulness not only towards their loved ones, but also towards God.
